reasoning_traces.think:
Perception is formalized as a Bayesian process where beliefs B evolve according to sensory evidence S and prior knowledge P(B). Hallucinations emerge as stable fixed points in this belief space when external stimuli vanish. Cognitive noise introduces uncertainty into this process, leading to threshold effects such as reduced reading speed. These primitives form a unified framework for modeling perception as a dynamic system with probabilistic inference and deterministic attractor behavior. The interplay between sensory input, internal noise, and belief structure defines both normal perception and pathological states like hallucinations.
